big_idea: Decoders HEAR sounds, MAP letters, BLEND, and READ.
learning_intention: We are learning to decode CVC words and read decodable text.
student_learning_goal: I can decode CVC words and read decodable text.
success_criteria: I can SEGMENT a CVC word into 3 sounds.
I can MATCH letters to sounds.
I can BLEND sounds into a word.
I can READ a decodable sentence.
lesson_specific_materials: Big Decoder Capstone Template (1 per child)
Sound Box Cards, Letter Cards, Picture Cards, Sentence Strips at 4 stations

minds_on.hook: Sounder + Blendy: Today is the BIG DECODER day! 4 stations, 4 jobs: HEAR, MAP, BLEND, READ.
minds_on.teacher_script:
Both characters at the carpet. 'Reader friends — you are now DECODERS! In 4 days you learned 4 jobs. Today you do all 4 at 4 stations.'

Review the 4 jobs.
- 'Job 1 — HEAR. Segment a word into sounds. Like Day 1 with Sounder.'
- 'Job 2 — MAP. Match a letter to its sound. Like Day 2 with Blendy.'
- 'Job 3 — BLEND. Slide sounds into a word. Like Day 3.'
- 'Job 4 — READ. Decode a sentence. Like Day 4.'

Demonstrate each station briefly:
- 'Station 1: Hear. Pick a picture, segment it. /c/-/a/-/t/.'
- 'Station 2: Map. Letter card to phoneme bubble.'
- 'Station 3: Blend. Build a word in the sound box, slide.'
- 'Station 4: Read. Decode a sentence strip.'

Show the Capstone Template. 'You record what you do at each station here.'

'Sounder + Blendy say — you have ALL the tools. Use them at each stop!'

Quick orientation. Show each station's location and materials. Children plan their order (any order — rotate when teacher signals).

steps.instruction: Hand out Capstone Templates. Each child rotates 4 stations, ~6-7 minutes each.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say: '4 stations. Rotate when I signal.'

steps.instruction: Station 1 (HEAR): pick 2 pictures, segment into 3 sounds, mark on template.
Station 2 (MAP): match 4 letter cards to phoneme bubbles on the template.
steps.teacher_prompt: Show: line from letter to sound.

steps.instruction: Station 3 (BLEND): build 2 CVC words in sound boxes; write them on the template.
Station 4 (READ): read 2 decodable sentence strips; circle CVC words on the template.
Circulate to record summative evidence on the rubric.
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each child. Score on the 5-row rubric.

differentiation.for_extending: Add Station 5: write a sentence using a Station 3 word.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Pre-write the first letter of each Station 3 word.
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk briskly between stations; sit-stand-sit at each.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Four signals: segments at Station 1; maps at Station 2; blends at Station 3; reads at Station 4.
formative_check.how_to_record: Score on the summative rubric (5 rows × 4 levels).

discussion_prompts: What was YOUR favourite job today?
What is one new word you decoded?
consolidation.exit_routine: Each child shares ONE: 'I decoded ___ today.' Class chants 'HOO knows the sounds? YOU do!' for the last time.

assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 5 captures all 3 expectations: B2.1 (Station 1), B2.2 (Stations 2-3), B2.3 (Stations 3-4).

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child can do every station individually but cannot connect the 4 jobs — repairing the integration trap at Grade 1
expanded_walkthrough.rationale: Common Grade-1 trap on capstone day: child segments fluently at Station 1, maps fluently at Station 2, blends fluently at Station 3, reads fluently at Station 4 — but cannot articulate that these are connected steps of one DECODING process. This signals procedural knowledge without conceptual integration. The fix is metacognitive: name the connection.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: End of capstone. Child has done all 4 stations correctly. Teacher asks 'how does Station 1 help you at Station 4?' Child shrugs.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Sounder asks — at Station 1 you HEARD sounds. At Station 4 you READ sentences. The sounds in your head become the words on the page. Same sounds!'

Probe. 'When you read CAT, what 3 sounds did you say? /c/-/a/-/t/. Same sounds you segmented at Station 1.'

Generalise. 'Sounder + Blendy say — HEAR, MAP, BLEND, READ are all the same brain job. Sounds in your ears, letters on the page, words in your mind.'

If the child doesn't connect: walk them backwards. 'You read CAT at Station 4. How? You blended /c/-/a/-/t/. How? You knew C says /c/ from Station 2. How did you know /c/ was a sound at all? Station 1.'
expected_student_responses: (Stretched) 'I HEAR sounds, I MAP letters to sounds, I BLEND, I READ.'
common_misconceptions: Each station is its own thing. (Repair: name the chain.)
Reading is different from sound work. (Repair: same sounds.)
recovery_moves: Walk backwards from Station 4 → 3 → 2 → 1, naming the connection at each step.
Use the unit poster's 4-step decoder process as a visual chain.
Have the child explain to a partner: 'I HEAR /c/, I see C, I BLEND, I READ.'
Celebrate the integration explicitly: 'You used ALL FOUR JOBS today. You are a real decoder.'

parts_outline.task: Hear + Map: 2 picture-and-sound-boxes; segment into sounds and write the letters.
Blend: 2 sound-box words; read aloud and write the word on the line.
Read: 2 short decodable sentences with circle-the-CVC-word task.
